PullRequest.Title: show full path for each mcp server
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335683

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the AI Customization MCP Servers section and render installed/available rows with provenance
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget synchronously filters cached server collections, resolves each row's source from cached observables/arrays, computes virtual-list heights, and renders visible rows. The pre-existing gallery snapshot request starts after the initial home render and is not required for installed rows to appear.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the first MCP gallery page through IMcpWorkbenchService.queryGallery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active snapshot request per cold visible widget state; a new request cancels the prior CTS, and a populated snapshot suppresses further cold loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same gallery snapshot request occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the installed-list render critical path; it only populates the Available section when complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N installed MCP rows, P discovered plugins, and E installed extensions. Provenance height/render resolution is in-memory; plugin/extension matching uses linear array scans, so worst-case CPU is proportional to N*(P+E), while DOM/hover creation remains bounded by virtualized visible rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source resolution is synchronous. Gallery loading permits one effective request because a replacement disposes the previous cancellation token source.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MCP definitions are cached observables, plugin discovery is a derived observable, and the extension service caches its local projection. Gallery results are held in gallerySnapshotServers; failed/active loads are tracked and requests are cancellation-replaced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that provenance adds bounded synchronous lookups and formatting but no filesystem, IPC, subprocess, or network boundary to list rendering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can install many extensions, but realistically only a small number of MCP rows require extension/plugin matching; there is no evidence that the added in-memory scans create measurable latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added work is bounded in-memory presentation work on a virtualized list, while the only network operation on this scenario is pre-existing and off the installed-row critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh, search, resize, and scroll the MCP server list as server/session state changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: State changes may rebuild the existing section lists; provenance is recalculated for inserted rows, and layout is coalesced to the next animation frame before width/height reads. Scrolling recycles only viewport templates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the MCP gallery for a non-empty user search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One debounced/cancellation-replaced request per settled search query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Search used the same gallery query path before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous; local installed-row filtering and rendering do not wait for the gallery response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with installed MCP row count on list rebuild and with visible row count while scrolling. Each visible template adds one source DOM node and managed hover; virtualization bounds live DOM nodes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Layout requests are coalesced through a single pending animation-frame disposable; gallery searches cancel superseded requests rather than accumulating concurrent calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached definition/plugin/extension data is reused. Gallery snapshot/search state and cancellation behavior are unchanged. No new retained map or unbounded cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the refresh listeners, list splice path, virtual delegate, and animation-frame layout path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The existing full-list rebuild frequency depends on MCP/session events, but the diff adds only source lookup/string/DOM updates per affected row and does not amplify boundary calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new expensive boundary or unbounded retention is introduced, and viewport DOM work remains virtualized and layout-coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate a plugin provenance link from an MCP row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single click opens the existing embedded plugin detail and starts README loading; the detail shell renders before the asynchronous README completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read README.md below the selected installed plugin URI (including remote-filesystem access for vscodeRemote).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read for the one explicitly selected plugin per detail render; no collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same plugin detail and README read were already reachable through the existing Show Plugin management action; this PR adds a direct provenance-link trigger.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The README subsection waits for the read, but navigation and the rest of the detail render proceed synchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected plugin and one README whose parse/render cost scales with that README's byte length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One read is launched per activation; generation checks prevent stale results from rendering, though the underlying existing read is not canceled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No README cache is used, but loading occurs only on explicit activation and stale render results are guarded by a generation token.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the new link reaches the existing detail loader and performs exactly one boundary read for an installed plugin.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: README size and remote filesystem latency vary, but activation is deliberate and singular.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is intentional user-triggered detail loading, not eager work or fan-out, and the same operation was already available through the row's management action.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate an extension provenance link from an MCP row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A single click calls IExtensionsWorkbenchService.open for the source extension and opens its MCP feature editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: If the extension ID cannot be found in the cached installed collection, fall back to a gallery getExtensions request before opening the editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero requests in the normal warm path because extension provenance is derived from an installed MCP collection; at most one gallery lookup for the selected ID on a cold/missing-cache fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no direct extension provenance link in the MCP row before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Editor opening awaits the fallback only when the installed extension cannot be resolved locally.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one extension ID per explicit activation; no per-server or per-extension fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited open operation per click; the changed code does not launch a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The normal path scans the ExtensionsWorkbenchService cached installed list. Only a cache miss reaches the gallery fallback.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-click call path and warm-cache behavior; low evidence that the fallback is prevalent enough to constitute a regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A transient initialization race could use the fallback, but the MCP collection source normally corresponds to an already installed extension and the service is eagerly initialized.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the operation is explicit, singular, and normally local; there is no realistic scaling or hot-path mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all five changed files and all diff pages. The PR adds bounded, virtualized provenance rendering and explicit navigation links; no high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
